summary: This bill prohibits the President from declaring a moratorium on hydraulic fracturing unless Congress passes a law authorizing it.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budget allocations. It focuses solely on regulatory authority over hydraulic fracturing.
No tax provisions, rate changes, credits, or revenue measures appear in the bill text.
The legislation addresses energy regulation and has no connection to healthcare policy, insurance, or medical services.
No references to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill does not address immigration, border policy, or related enforcement.
No content related to reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions concerning military budgets, defense programs, or armed forces.

The bill explicitly prohibits a presidential moratorium on hydraulic fracturing without congressional approval and affirms state primacy over regulation of fracking on state and private lands. Hydraulic fracturing is frequently targeted by environmental regulations due to concerns over emissions, water contamination, and climate impacts. By blocking federal moratoriums, the legislation protects continued use of this extraction method and thereby limits the scope of environmental restrictions on fossil fuel production.
